stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When engineers dismantled a 1920s railway trestle in Ohio, they expected its timber pilings, which had sat underwater for nearly a century, to be badly weakened. Core samples showed the pilings to be anything but ______: they kept almost all of their original load-bearing strength. The oxygen-poor mud around them had apparently kept decay-causing fungi from growing.
explanation: Start with what the evidence shows: the pilings kept almost all of their strength. The phrase "anything but" reverses the blank, so the blank has to mean the opposite of strong. "Degraded" fits. The pilings were anything but degraded, which is why the engineers' expectation of weakness turned out wrong.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence (the strength the pilings kept) and skipped the reversal. "Anything but durable" would mean the pilings were weak, which is the opposite of what the core samples showed.

C.why: The passage says the pilings sat underwater for nearly a century. Calling them "anything but submerged" denies a fact the text states outright.

D.why: The passage never mentions upgrades or modernization. The test results after the colon are about strength, so they give no support for a claim about modernizing.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Some seismologists have dismissed the faint tremors that sometimes come before large earthquakes as ______, little more than random background noise in the Earth's crust. A 2025 analysis of 300 earthquakes along the Chilean coast challenges this view. In the days before 70 percent of those earthquakes, the tremors followed a consistent pattern, which suggests they may carry real information about an approaching rupture.
explanation: The blank sits inside the view that the passage then knocks down. The phrase "little more than random background noise" restates it, so the blank has to mean something like unimportant. "Inconsequential" fits. The new analysis challenges that dismissal by showing the tremors may matter after all.

A.why: You took what the new evidence shows (the tremors may carry information) and put it into the dismissive view. That is the opposite of the view the passage describes. Nobody calls something "little more than random background noise" because it is predictive.

C.why: How often the tremors occur is beside the point. The dismissive view is about whether they mean anything, and "frequent" does not restate "little more than random background noise."

D.why: The passage calls the tremors faint. Dismissing them as destructive clashes with that description and with the idea that they are just noise.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Historians have long praised the 1570s maps of Flemish engraver Pieter Vanmolen for their careful craftsmanship. But a recent comparison with satellite imagery suggests that the maps lacked ______. On them, coastlines are misplaced by as much as 40 kilometers, and several rivers run through the wrong valleys.
explanation: Start with the evidence: the coastlines and rivers are badly misplaced. The word "lacked" reverses the blank, so the blank names the quality the maps did not have. Maps with errors of 40 kilometers lacked precision.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence (the maps are full of errors) and skipped the reversal. "Lacked distortion" would mean the maps were accurate, which is the exact opposite of what the satellite comparison found.

B.why: Ornament has nothing to do with misplaced coastlines and rivers. The evidence after the blank is about accuracy, not how the maps look.

D.why: The passage says nothing about how widely the maps were distributed. Misplaced rivers are evidence that the maps were inaccurate, not that few people saw them.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Woodblock prints are made by pressing paper against a single inked block, so art historians once assumed that impressions pulled from the same block would be virtually identical. However, when conservator Hana Ostrowski examined 40 surviving impressions of a 1790s landscape print, she found striking differences in ink density and line width from sheet to sheet. Her findings make it unlikely that the block's output was ever truly ______.
explanation: The evidence shows that the impressions differ noticeably. "Unlikely … ever truly" reverses the blank, so the blank has to be the opposite of differing. "Uniform" fits, and it echoes the older assumption that the prints were "virtually identical," which Ostrowski's findings undercut.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence (the sheets differ) and skipped the "unlikely" reversal. Saying it is unlikely the output was ever inconsistent would mean the prints matched, which is the opposite of what Ostrowski found.

B.why: Whether collectors wanted the prints never comes up. The findings are about how similar the impressions are, not about their market appeal.

C.why: Differences in ink density and line width say nothing about how many colors the print used. You would need evidence the passage doesn't give to rule out a single-color print.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Some climate researchers have predicted that rising winter temperatures will make heavy snowfall less ______ around North America's Great Lakes. Yet warmer lakes stay unfrozen later into the season and release more moisture into the cold air that passes over them. Weather records from Buffalo, New York, show that major lake-effect snowstorms have struck more often since 1950, not less.
explanation: The blank sits inside a prediction that the passage then knocks down with "Yet." The Buffalo records show snowstorms becoming more frequent, so the prediction being challenged must say snowfall would become less frequent. "Less common" says that, and the evidence that storms have "struck more often" contradicts it.

A.why: You matched the blank to what the evidence shows (more storms) and forgot the "less" in front of it. "Less rare" means more frequent, which would make the prediction agree with the Buffalo data instead of being contradicted by it.

B.why: Snow already falls only in certain seasons, and the evidence after "Yet" is about how often storms strike, not when in the year they arrive. "Less seasonal" doesn't set up the contrast the passage draws.

C.why: The passage gives no evidence about forecasting. A rise in how often storms strike doesn't refute a claim about predictability, so "Yet" would have nothing to push against.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Many growers clear crop residue from their fields after harvest, reasoning that the leftover stalks shelter insects through the winter. A three-year trial in Iowa, however, found that plots left covered hosted far more ground beetles, which eat pest larvae, and ended each season with fewer crop-damaging insects than cleared plots did. The findings therefore challenge the assumption that residue ______ pest populations.
explanation: The trial shows that residue leads to fewer pests. The sentence says the findings challenge an assumption, so the blank has to hold the growers' old belief, which is the opposite of what the trial found. Growers thought residue shelters insects, so they assumed it bolsters (builds up) pest populations. The trial challenges that.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence and skipped the reversal. The trial does show residue curbs pests, but the findings 'challenge the assumption,' so the blank must be the belief that was overturned, not the result.

C.why: You may have connected 'reveals' to the beetles found in covered plots. But the passage is about whether residue raises or lowers pest numbers, not whether it makes them visible.

D.why: You may have linked 'outlasts' to residue staying on the field over the winter. Residue outliving a population has nothing to do with the growers' belief that it shelters insects.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Historians once regarded the indigo-dyed cloth traded along West Africa's coast in the 1700s as little more than a ______ commodity, valued only for its price. explanation: The letters show that buyers cared about who made the cloth and how well it was patterned. That evidence knocks down the historians' older view, and the blank sits inside that older view. 'Little more than' and 'valued only for its price' tell you the historians saw the cloth as interchangeable. 'Generic' says exactly that.

A.why: You took the blank from the merchant letters, which show the cloth was distinctive. But the blank describes the view the letters overturn. 'Little more than a distinctive commodity, valued only for its price' contradicts itself.

B.why: You picked a word about cloth as a physical material. The passage is about whether buyers told one cloth from another, not about how durable it was.

D.why: The passage says the cloth was traded and bought openly, so historians could not have thought it was forbidden.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Because the virus alters its surface proteins every season, researchers expected antibodies produced in response to last year's vaccine to be largely useless against the new strain. Laboratory tests showed otherwise: the older antibodies still attached to a stable region of the protein and slowed infection in cell cultures. The team concluded that prior vaccination is unlikely to be as ______ against new strains as earlier models suggested.
explanation: The tests show that old antibodies still help. The earlier models predicted they would be 'largely useless.' The sentence says prior vaccination is 'unlikely to be as ___ as earlier models suggested,' so the blank has to be what the models claimed. That is 'futile,' meaning useless. Read it back: vaccination is unlikely to be as futile as the models suggested. That matches the lab result.

B.why: You matched the blank to the lab result (the antibodies protect) and skipped 'unlikely to be as … as.' Saying vaccination is unlikely to be as protective as the models suggested would mean the models were too optimistic, but they actually predicted it would be useless.

C.why: You matched the topic. 'Contagious' fits a sentence about viruses, but vaccination is not contagious, and the passage is about whether old antibodies still work.

D.why: The passage never mentions cost. The models and the lab tests disagree only about how well prior vaccination works.

explanation: The evidence shows the mapmakers knew the inland regions well, since the same workshops drew detailed inland maps. The sentence says the sparseness 'does not imply' something, so the blank is the conclusion the evidence rules out: that the mapmakers did not know the interior. That is ignorance. 'Then' tells you this sentence sums up the argument just made.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence (the mapmakers had real inland knowledge) and dropped the 'not.' 'Does not imply expertise' would back the scholars' claim that the passage is arguing against.

B.why: You may have noticed the workshops serving 'other clients.' The argument is about what the mapmakers knew, not how generous they were.

C.why: Nothing in the passage mentions competition between workshops. The blank has to name the conclusion some scholars drew from the empty interiors.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: For much of the twentieth century, coaches regarded long static stretches before a sprint as ______ to performance and made them a fixed part of every pre-race routine. A review of controlled trials published in 2019 has challenged that view: across the studies it examined, sprinters who held stretches for thirty seconds or more just before running posted slower times than sprinters who warmed up with light jogging alone.
explanation: The blank is inside the view that the review challenged. The evidence shows that stretching made sprinters slower, so the view it knocks down is the opposite: the belief that stretching helped. 'Conducive to performance' means 'helping performance', and that also explains why coaches made stretching a fixed part of every routine. Read the full sentence back with 'challenged that view' in it and it holds together.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence and skipped the reversal. 'Detrimental' (harmful) is what the review found. The blank holds the coaches' belief, which the review 'challenged', so it has to be the opposite of what the review found.

C.why: 'Immaterial' means the stretches made no difference. Coaches would not make something that made no difference a fixed part of every routine, so this clashes with the first sentence.

D.why: 'Comparable to performance' says nothing about whether stretching helps or hurts, and that effect is the whole point of the sentence. The phrase also isn't natural English for describing an effect.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: In 2020, as offices emptied, some labour economists predicted that the shift to working from home would prove ______. Data from the years that followed lend little support to that prediction. The share of paid workdays performed at home fell from its pandemic peak, but it settled at roughly four times its pre-2020 level and has stayed close to that figure for three consecutive years.
explanation: First, say what the data show: working from home stayed high for years. Then apply the reversal. The data 'lend little support to' the prediction, so the prediction must have been the opposite of lasting. 'Transient' means short-lived, and that is the claim the steady three-year figure undercuts.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence and skipped the reversal. The data show the shift was enduring, which means 'enduring' is the claim the data support. The prediction in the blank is one the data fail to support.

B.why: A level four times higher than before 2020 shows the shift was widespread, so the data confirm this prediction. The text says the data lend it little support, so 'widespread' reverses the relationship the text sets up.

D.why: The data are about how many workdays happen at home over time. They say nothing about profit, so they could neither support nor undercut a prediction about profitability.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When the city of Halvern widened its ring road from four lanes to six in 2008, officials expected rush-hour travel times to fall. Five years later, the road carried 30 percent more vehicles, and average commutes were no shorter than before construction began. explanation: The evidence shows that widening the road did not shorten commutes. 'Far from' reverses the blank, so the blank is what the project failed to be: what its backers promised, a fix for congestion. 'Remedy' means a cure or fix. Read back in full, 'far from the remedy its backers had promised' matches the first sentence, where officials expected travel times to fall.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence and skipped 'far from'. A stalemate, where nothing improved, is what the project turned out to be. The blank names the thing the project was far from, and no backer would promise a stalemate.

C.why: 'Detour' fits the topic of roads, but nothing in the passage is about rerouting traffic. You picked a word that sounds like road planning instead of the word that does the job in this sentence.

D.why: Whether the road became a landmark has nothing to do with travel times. The evidence after the colon is about congestion, so it can't show the project falling short of being a landmark.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Engineers have long assumed that adding glass fibers to recycled polypropylene makes it much stiffer than the same plastic left unreinforced. When materials scientist Rosa Iturbe's team placed identical loads on both versions, however, the reinforced samples bent only about 4 percent less than the plain ones. explanation: The evidence shows that the gap between the two materials is small: the reinforced samples bent only about 4 percent less. The sentence says the difference is "far less ______ than engineers have assumed," so the blank must name what engineers expected, which was a large difference. "Pronounced" means large or clearly noticeable. Read it back with the negative in place: the difference is far less pronounced than assumed. That matches the evidence.

B.why: You matched the blank to the evidence and skipped the reversal. The difference really is negligible, but "far less negligible than assumed" would mean the gap is bigger than expected, which is the opposite of what the test found.

C.why: You chose a word that fits the topic of materials under load. The blank describes the size of the difference between the two materials, not how either one springs back, so "far less elastic" says nothing about the gap.

D.why: You added an idea about time that the passage never raises. Nothing in the text says how long the difference lasts. The study measured only how large the difference is.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

B.why: You matched the topic, since selkies are sea creatures in island stories. The sentence is about whether the two traditions are connected to each other, and the motif comparison has nothing to say about whether the stories are maritime.

D.why: You read in a claim about age that the passage never makes. Dahl compared plot motifs, not dates, so her findings could not challenge a view about when the traditions began.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Historians have often claimed that cochineal, an imported red dye made from insects, quickly replaced locally grown madder in Flemish weaving workshops after 1600. Yet when chemist Pieter Hoeks analyzed 300 red fabric fragments made in those workshops between 1600 and 1650, he detected madder in 184 of them and cochineal in only 23. Hoeks's findings indicate that during this period, cochineal was unlikely to have been ______ in the workshops.
explanation: The evidence shows a wide gap: madder appears in eight times as many fragments as cochineal. The sentence says cochineal was "unlikely to have been ______," so the blank must be the opposite of what the counts show. Cochineal was the minority dye, so it was unlikely to have been predominant. Read it back with the negative: cochineal was unlikely to have been predominant. That agrees with 23 fragments compared with 184.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence and dropped "unlikely to have been." Cochineal really was scarce, so saying it was unlikely to have been scarce reverses the finding. This choice is the opposite of the answer.

B.why: You picked a word that suits red dye, which is a topic match. Hoeks counted how often each dye appears. His counts say nothing about how bright cochineal's color was.

C.why: You assumed something about price that the passage never mentions. Fragment counts show how widely a dye was used, not what it cost, so they can't support a claim that cochineal was cheap.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Biologists once described the hermit crab Pagurus vasilis as ______ in its choice of shells, assuming that it simply moved into the first empty shell it came across. explanation: The blank names the old description that Nasser's trials 'undercut,' and the next clause defines it: the crab 'simply moved into the first empty shell it came across.' B.why: Hermit crabs defending space is a real behavior, but the passage is about how the crab chooses a shell. 'Territorial' doesn't fit 'the first empty shell it came across.'

C.why: Nothing in the passage is about when the crab is active. You picked a word that fits the marine-biology topic instead of what the sentence says about choosing shells.
